subject: Clarify: geographic restore windows & retention rollback language
messages:
From: Ethan Russo <ethan.russo@aurumhealth.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal@aurumhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Questions on restore / rollback language in DPA

Hi Chloe,

Thanks for sending the latest DPA redline. We're reviewing but have a couple of specific operational clarifications we need before we can sign:

1) Restore window & geographic scope — Section 4.2 currently says "we retain snapshots for 90 days and may retain backups for up to 365 days in a different region". Can you confirm whether Aurora-specific restores (customer-initiated full restores) can be served from the onshore region only, or whether Redwood may trigger cross-region restores as part of disaster recovery? Our regulator expects restores to be initiated only from within our chosen jurisdiction unless we opt into cross-border DR.

2) Retention rollback / reversal requests — if Aurum requests a rollback (e.g., reinstate a dataset version that had been scheduled for deletion), what is the guaranteed timeframe to respond and are there any conditions that could prevent such a rollback (legal hold, export restrictions, snapshot immutability)?

3) Backups & secondary copies — do secondary offline copies fall under the same "deletion upon request" obligations? If we accept a redline that asks for deletion of customer data within X days, will offline retention (tape/third-party escrow) be included or excluded?

I've attached our annotated redline (Aurum_DPA_redline_v3.docx) and a short playbook we drafted to show how our compliance team expects restores to be documented (restore-playbook-appendix.pdf).

Can you loop in whoever owns the operational side for restores so we can get a concrete answer to (1) and (2)?

Cheers,
Ethan
Ethan Russo
Head of Compliance, Aurum Health

From: Chloe Martin <chloe@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Russo <ethan.russo@aurumhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Legal Ops <legal@aurumhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 13:04:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Questions on restore / rollback language in DPA

Hi Ethan — thanks for the clear notes and the attachments. Looping in Karthik (serving/runtime) and Laura (legal) to help with the operational and contract language.

High-level answers up front:
- Cross-region restores are allowed only under two conditions: (a) you opt-in in the DPA Annex with the explicit geography clause, or (b) a survivability incident requires DR and we notify you and offer the onshore restore first. By default, we will serve customer-requested restores from the chosen onshore region.
- Rollback requests: we can attempt a rollback if the requested snapshot exists and is not subject to a legal hold or retention mandated by law. Operational SLA for a rollback-confirmation is 5 business days; actual restore completion depends on size and can be queued under our dedicated capacity rules.
- Offline/secondary copies: these are considered part of our backup footprint. Deletion requests will cascade to offline copies within the documented retention windows, except where we have a contractual exception (e.g., archival escrow required by law).

I want to be explicit in redline language rather than high-level statements — Karthik, can you draft a short operational clause we can propose to replace 4.2 and the rollback paragraph? Laura, if you could also suggest the exact sentence-level contract language on opt-in and notification, that would be great.

Thanks,
Chloe
Chloe Martin
Principal Account Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe@redwood.com>, Ethan Russo <ethan.russo@aurumhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Legal Ops <legal@aurumhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 16:22:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Questions on restore / rollback language in DPA

Ethan, Chloe — quick technical write-up to support the contract language below.

Operational proposal (technical behavior):
- Snapshot retention: primary snapshots are retained for 90 days in the customer-selected region.
- Secondary (replicated) backups: for durability we maintain a secondary encrypted copy in a geographically-separated region for up to 365 days unless the customer opts out. Secondary copies are used strictly for disaster recovery and internal integrity checks.
- Customer-initiated restore: if Aurum initiates a restore via the console or support request, we will attempt to execute the restore from the primary (onshore) snapshot. If the primary snapshot is unavailable (hardware failure or region outage), Redwood will notify Aurum and may use the secondary copy in the DR region to perform the restore; such cross-region restores require explicit opt-in in the DPA Annex unless Redwood exercises its incident DR fallback and provides notice within 48 hours of action.
- Rollback requests: if a rollback targets a snapshot that is present and not flagged for legal hold, Redwood will acknowledge the request within 5 business days and provide an estimated completion date. For datasets larger than 10 TB, restores may follow a prioritized queue determined by the customer's committed capacity or purchase of expedited restore hours.
- Deletion propagation: deletion requests that pass validation will be applied to primary and secondary copies; for offline archival (escrow) copies held by third parties, Redwood will coordinate deletion requests and provide certification only if deletion is actionable under the third-party's contract.

Suggested redline sentence (for insertion in DPA):
"Customer-selected-region: Redwood will retain primary snapshots within the customer-selected geographic region for a minimum of 90 days. Secondary encrypted copies may be retained in a geographically-separated recovery region for up to 365 days for disaster-recovery purposes; the customer may opt out of cross-region replication by executing the Geographic Replication Opt-Out Annex. Customer-initiated restores will, by default, be performed from the primary snapshot in the customer-selected region. In the event the primary snapshot is unavailable due to an infrastructure or availability incident, Redwood may, after providing notice to Customer, restore from the geographically-separated recovery copy to meet recovery objectives.

Rollback requests: Redwood will acknowledge valid rollback or restoration requests within five (5) business days and will use commercially reasonable efforts to complete a requested restoration; actual restoration timelines depend on dataset size and queueing. Restorations will not be performed if the snapshot is subject to a lawful hold or other legal restriction.

Deletion and archival copies: Deletion requests accepted by Redwood will be applied to primary and secondary backup copies in accordance with the applicable retention schedule. Deletion of third-party escrow or offline archival copies will be subject to the third party's deletion process; Redwood will coordinate and provide certification where possible."

Happy to iterate on wording; putting this in plain language so Laura can tighten it for legal.

–Karthik

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Russo <ethan@redwood.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Legal Ops <legal@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Questions on restore / rollback language in DPA

Ethan — thanks for the patience. We've reviewed Karthik's operational proposal and updated the redline in your document. Key contract edits we've proposed (high level):

1) Added a short "Geographic Replication Opt-Out Annex" clause so your compliance team can explicitly opt out of cross-border secondary copies.
2) Clarified that Redwood's DR fallback is permitted only when the primary region is demonstrably unavailable and Redwood provides written notice within forty-eight (48) hours of any cross-region restore action.
3) Defined "acknowledge" as a contractual SLA (five business days) and "use commercially reasonable efforts" for the restore completion obligation; if restoration timelines are critical, we added optional "expedited restore services" as a billable addendum with defined throughput.
4) Deletion and certification: deletion of primary and internal secondary backups is part of the standard deletion workflow; deletion of third-party escrow or offline archival copies will be handled by Redwood with reasonable cooperation but may be subject to the third party's deletion window. Redwood will provide a deletion certificate for all copies it controls within the timeframe described.

We've attached the updated redline in the HubSpot link included above and also attached a short certificate template. If that aligns with Aurum's compliance needs, can you confirm acceptance of the Opt-Out Annex or propose any changes? If you accept, we can prepare the final DPA for signature and add the expedite-restore addendum as an optional clause on the signature page.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
